meaning: The build finished (or was skipped) but Netlify can't find the folder it's supposed to publish. Your publish directory setting and the folder your build actually creates don't match.
causes: Vite outputs dist, but Netlify is set to build (CRA) or out (Next export), or the other way around.
The project is in a subfolder (e.g. frontend/) and Base directory is not set.
The build command is empty, so nothing gets built.
The build failed earlier and the real error is higher up in the log.

steps.text: Scroll up in the deploy log and make sure the build itself succeeded.
Run npm run build locally and see which folder appears (dist for Vite, build for Create React App).
Set Site configuration > Build & deploy: Base directory (if in a subfolder), Build command npm run build, Publish directory dist. Or in netlify.toml:
steps.code:
[build]
  base = "frontend"   # only if the app lives in a subfolder
  command = "npm run build"
  publish = "dist"     # relative to base

steps.text: Trigger a new deploy with 'Clear cache and deploy site'.

prompt: Netlify fails with "Deploy directory 'dist' does not exist". Check which folder our build script outputs, where package.json lives, and write a netlify.toml with the correct base, command and publish values.

faq.q: Can I just commit the dist folder?
faq.a: You can drag-and-drop deploy it, but letting Netlify build is easier to keep updated.
Don't set publish to out unless you use static export; Netlify's Next.js runtime handles it.
